documented_warnings: Phil.3.12 purpose reading and Christ’s prior initiative
Phil.3.14 relationship between the prize and God’s upward call

verse_renderings.text: I do not mean that I have already reached the goal or am already complete. But I keep pressing on to take hold of the purpose for which Christ Jesus first took hold of me.
Brothers and sisters, I do not consider myself to have taken hold of the goal yet. But I focus on one thing: I leave what lies behind and stretch toward what lies ahead.
I press on toward the goal to win the prize that comes with God’s upward call in Christ Jesus.
So all of us who are mature should share this mindset. And if you think differently about anything, God will make even that clear to you.
In any case, we must keep living in a way that matches how far we have already come.

reader_notes.text: The Greek does not state what Paul has not yet obtained. The context points to the goal described in verses 10–11 and developed through the race imagery in verses 13–14.

reader_notes.anchor: the purpose for which Christ Jesus first took hold of me
reader_notes.text: The Greek repeats a verb meaning “take hold of.” The phrase may mean that Paul pursues the purpose for which Christ took hold of him, as translated here, or that he pursues because Christ took hold of him. The word “first” makes Christ’s prior action explicit.

The Greek compactly speaks of “the prize of God’s upward call in Christ Jesus.” The phrase may describe God’s call drawing believers upward or His heavenly call. The reading text follows the upward-direction sense and expresses the prize as coming with that call.
The words translated “complete” in verse 12 and “mature” in verse 15 come from the same Greek root. Paul creates a deliberate tension: mature believers recognize that they have not yet arrived.

reader_notes.anchor: living in a way that matches how far we have already come
reader_notes.text: The final Greek verb can picture walking in line or keeping in step. The reading text expresses this as living consistently with the progress believers have already made.
